Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal ran a pass on Exhibit B and came back with a couple of redline items we need clarified before procurement can sign. High level: the current Exhibit language is ambiguous about whether the caps/floors and tier thresholds apply at the individual SKU level, per-bundle, or across the aggregate usage of Novus. In practice Novus plans to move some workloads between packaged SKUs and burst capacity over the term, and our finance team needs the billing behavior to be clear for true-ups.

We attached our annotated Exhibit B (Novus_ExhibitB_Redline_070428.docx). Key asks:
- Is the floor/calculation "per SKU" or "portfolio-wide"?
- If portfolio-wide, how are credits/overages allocated to an invoice line?
- Suggested fallback if Redwood introduces a new SKU mid-term: will the new SKU inherit the same tier linkage?

Can you please send any proposed contract language and an operational mapping we can share with finance? We are trying to close this week.

Thanks,
Alicia Torres

Quick answers up front:
1) Redwood's intent: tiers and caps in Exhibit B are intended to operate portfolio-wide (aggregate across SKUs) unless an SKU is explicitly called out as "standalone" in the Order Schedule. That prevents per-SKU fragmentation when customers move workloads between our optimized SKUs.
2) Allocation method: for billing we allocate usage to the SKU line items based on the customer's month-to-date usage mix. Can you confirm whether Novus requires an invoice-level line-item breakdown by original purchase SKU for audit, or if an aggregate invoice with a reconciliation workbook is acceptable?

- An operational workbook (tier_mapping_matrix_070528.xlsx) showing worked examples (monthly and quarterly true-up).

Subject: Internal: proposed Exhibit B language + mapping (technical)

Priya / Marissa — technical note and proposed wording we should commit to in the redline. This is focused on operational behavior so Procurement/legal can rely on it.

Summary of behavior implemented in our billing engine:
- Aggregation: usage is aggregated at customer-account level for tier calculations. Tiers/thresholds in Exhibit B apply on aggregate usage, not per-SKU, unless SKU is marked "isolated" in the Order Schedule.
- Allocation for invoices: we bill by SKU line items for visibility, but credits/overages are computed on the aggregated tier result. The invoice will include a reconciliation section showing per-SKU usage and how the aggregate tier produced the final charge.
- New SKUs mid-term: new SKUs default to "linked" behavior and are included in aggregation for existing tiers. Customers may opt to classify a SKU as "standalone" (requires Amendment).

Proposed contract insertion (single paragraph to add to Exhibit B, redline ready):
"For purposes of the Pricing Schedule and any associated caps, floors, or tiered thresholds, usage shall be aggregated at the Customer Account level and applied against the Pricing Schedule tiers on an account-wide basis. Individual Order Schedule line items shall reflect billed units for observability; however final charges, credits, and true-up calculations shall be determined based on account-wide aggregated usage unless a given SKU is expressly designated as 'Standalone SKU' in the Order Schedule. New SKUs introduced during the Term shall be treated as linked to existing tiers by default unless the Parties expressly agree otherwise in an Amendment."

I also attached tier_mapping_matrix_070528.xlsx with two worked scenarios (monthly migration from SKU-A to SKU-B and an end-of-quarter true-up with a new SKU introduced mid-quarter). Can we get legal to rubber-stamp this language and decide on invoice presentation (aggregate invoice + reconciliation sheet vs separate line-level true-ups)?

-Karthik
Principal Product Ops — Redwood Inference
